system.summary: Invented signs (Greek-like letters, figure-like signs) for letters; 23 signs; two signs each for e, r and b; g is a joined oo; i/j and u/v one sign each; word breaks mostly kept; code numbers in figures (59, 60, 68) inside the cipher.
system.notes: Key found ciphertext-only and frozen after letter 1 p. 2. Nomenclator: three code numbers written as figures (60, 59, 68); in letter 1, 4 occurrences of these 3 distinct numbers (60 once, 59 twice, 68 once); in letter 2 so far 59 once. None is identified.

diacritics.note: A small cross over the delta-shaped sign (D) appears in some words and not in the same word elsewhere; it is not treated as a mark (SIGN_CONVENTIONS.md).

prior_solution.where: Two web searches (12 Nov 2026) and the catalogue vetting of 11 Nov 2026 (DECODE, Cryptiana, HistoCrypt) found nothing on these letters.

conditions.human_role: WAINUT set the task (catalogue 2532) and the rules; AI language-model agents transcribed, found and froze the key, ran the held-out test and read. No human palaeographer or historian checked the text.
tools: scripts in this folder (fetch, crop, decryption, mark check)
models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT), viewing the images

solution.what: 8 scans fetched at full size through the archieven.nl viewer (Zoomify tiles, one request at a time).
Sign conventions written before any value; letter 1 p. 2 pass 1 from 1.5x crops; pass 2 after the key hypothesis (not blind).
Crib 'Monsieur l'ambassadeur' from the pattern of the 12-sign word after the clear 'Monsieur', then common words; key frozen after p. 2.
Letter 1 pp. 1 and 3 and the first eight cipher lines of letter 2 decrypted with the frozen key: 54 of 58 words French in context, 1 wrong, 3 holes.
Letter 1 read with every departure marked; check_marks.py PASS; 154 of 165 cipher words verbatim (93.3%); Dan's checker 13 of 17 sentences clean on the running text.

Integration check (round 7, 13 Nov 2026): check_marks.py, signs.py and the checkers re-run (154 of 165 = 93.3% verbatim reproduced); own second decoder from key_frozen.tsv matches decryption_malen1.txt on all 33 lines; scan 2 fetched from the archive viewer's Zoomify tiles, and the line layout and word counts of L07-L10 agree (not a sign-by-sign blind transcription). Strict share stays 154 of 165 = 93.3%; with the 4 unresolved code-number occurrences (60, 59 twice, 68) as holes 154 of 169 = 91.1%. Letter 2 Dutch passages and a blind transcription are workable, so the target stays in progress.

outcome.method_basis: No key or gloss. The key was found from a crib suggested by the clear 'Monsieur' and by word patterns, frozen, and tested on held-out passages of both letters. All 23 signs that occur have a value; the three code numbers (60, 59, 68) are not identified, so the key is recorded as partial.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Letter 1 (about 30 of the about 49 cipher lines) read in part; of letter 2, the first 8 lines decoded only.

texts.label: Letter 1, 28 December (French)
texts.summary: The Jülich dispute will be settled only by arms; it is a mistake to think 60 or 59 will let themselves be crowned by 68; threats to break the truce do not frighten 'us', and 'our camp waits for nothing else'; the restitution of [Rees]; the embassies of the baron [Anholt] called inventions of 'those gentlemen of Holland'; the league of the marquis of Brandenburg; errands with the Spanish ambassador; a safe-conduct and letters of recommendation. Dated in cipher 'De Londres'.
texts.note: 165 cipher words: 154 verbatim from the signs, 3 with a marked repair, 3 guesses, 5 holes (93.3%). The clear script was read only to place the cipher.

reading_review.note: The cipher passages form coherent French throughout, with holes and guesses marked and carried into the English; signs spot-checked on the scans for seven lines (about 200 signs, no value-changing disagreement), and check_marks.py, the held-out test and _check_reading.py (13 of 17 sentences clean on the running text) reproduced. Read in part: three names are guesses (Rees, Anholt, sieges), five words are holes, the clear script is provisional, and a second blind transcription is still open.

texts.label: Letter 2, 21 October (French and Dutch): first cipher lines only
texts.summary: Opening: news passed to 'monsieur l'ambassadeur de 59', who will pay 12 florins a month to a person, provided he sends news every week. The Dutch passages are not yet transcribed.
texts.note: Only 8 of about 19 cipher lines transcribed (one pass); 36 of 37 words French in context with the frozen key.
